DEVELOPMENT PL AN REVIEW BO ARD
  MINUTES
  MARCH 23, 2023 at 8:30 AM
  245 EAST BONITA AVENUE
  COUNCIL CONFERENCE ROOM

  BOARD MEMBERS PRESENT

  David Bratt, Planning Commission
  Scott Dilley, Chamber of Commerce
  John Sorcinelli, Public Member at Large
  Brad McKinney, Assistant City Manager
  Steve Barragan, Engineering Manager (Substitute for Shari Garwick)
  Henry Noh, Director of Community Development

  STAFF PRESENT

  Luis Torrico, Planning Manager
  Anne Nguyen, Associate Planner
  James Miclat, Planning Intern
  Victoria Gutierrez, Departmental Assistant

CALL TO ORDER

David Bratt called the regular meeting of the Developmental Plan Review Board to order at 8:30
a.m. so as to conduct regular business in the Council Conference Room.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Director of Community Development Noh moved, seconded by Engineering Manager
Barragan to approve the October 13, 2022 Development Plan Review Board minutes. Motion
carried 4-0-2 (Dilley and Sorcinelli abstain).

DPRB Case No. 21-0002 & Tree Permit 21-0004
Associated Cases: ACCELA PROJ 21-0006, Zone Change 21-0001, Lot Merger 21-0001 & Initial
Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration

The Applicant, Ignacio Crespo, OC Design & Engineering, is requesting to develop a new 63,749
square-foot concrete tilt-up warehouse/office multi-tenant building and a Tree Removal Permit to
remove 17 mature trees on an existing 2.58-acre site.

The Applicant, Ignacio Crespo, was present.

Associate Planner Nguyen presented the staff report. She clarified, at the Board’s request, that
the occupants of properties were notified of the proposed project and the last tenant moved out
recently. She noted that only 2 mature trees will be preserved, one on the Northeast corner of the
lot and the other along Cataract Ave. She also noted that the proposed towers are recessed 4
 DPRB Minutes  Page 2
March 23, 2023

feet, the parapets will wrap around at a minimum of 10 feet, and the overall height of the building
is 41 feet.

Planning Manager Torrico added that there are no height limits on buildings for the proposed
M-1 Zone, however Staff worked with the Applicant to ensure the project would be compatible
with the surrounding neighborhood.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked if are any other buildings of the same height on that street.

Engineering Manager Barragan noted Organic Milling at 505 West Allen Avenue.

Mr. Sorcinelli stated that building is set farther back than the proposed building.

Associate Planner Nguyen stated the proposed building is set back 25 feet from Allen Avenue,
about 5 feet farther back than the existing homes and about as high as the power poles along
Allen and Cataract Avenue.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked what tenant will be using a warehouse of this height.

Associate Planner Nguyen stated the Applicant does not have a tenant at this time. She added
there will be a mezzanine level.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked if Staff discussed a lower height with the Applicant.

Associate Planner Nguyen answered that Staff worked with the Applicant but the additional
height is due to the parapets.

Planning Manager Torrico added that Staff has had many discussions with the applicant about
the overall design of the building, including the height, but what the Applicant proposed is what
they feel is adequate for their prospective tenants. The proposed height of the building is also
compliant with City Code and compatible with the surrounding industrial neighborhood.

Mr. Sorcinelli stated he is concerned about the residential homes across the street from the
project site. The height of the proposed building may raise an issue if it blocks their current view
of the mountains.

Associate Planner Nguyen concluded the staff report and recommended the Board recommend
approval to the Planning Commission subject to the conditions of approval.

Director of Community Development Noh stated the City does not have a scenic view
protection ordinance and the General Plan names the project site as industrial.

Associate Planner Nguyen stated the current zoning of the project site is Light Agricultural but
the Applicant is proposing a zone change to Light Manufacturing, making it consistent with the
General Plan.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked if Staff has heard from the residents across the street from the site about
the project.
 DPRB Minutes  Page 3
March 23, 2023

Associate Planner Nguyen answered a few residents had reached out to Staff to ask when the
homes would be demolished due to issues with trespassing, and she heard from nearby business
owners who supported the design of the project. She stated she may have heard from one
resident with concerns about the height of the proposed building early on in the process but has
not heard from them since.

Planning Manager Torrico clarified that the parapets that are adding to the overall height of the
building are intended to conceal rooftop equipment.

Director of Community Development Noh asked if there are proposed down lights above all
archways and recessed lighting where the proposed trellises are located.

Associate Planner Nguyen answered that is correct, and all will be downward lighting to avoid
spilling.

Mr. Bratt asked what the height of the walls in between the three parapets on the South Elevation
are.

Planning Manager Torrico answered the height is 38 feet.

Mr. Bratt recalled a past proposal of a three-story storage building that the Board denied due to
concerns about the height and stated this may be the same issue.

Associate Planner Nguyen stated that was a different development.

Director of Community Development Noh stated the Applicant may address the Board’s
concerns about the height of the building.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked if Cataract Avenue will be improved as part of the project.

Engineering Manager Barragan answered that it is part of the conditions that the Developer
improve the street to the center line and the City may consider improving the rest.

Mr. Sorcinelli stated such improvements would be important due to the damage heavy trucks
may cause to the East side of Cataract Avenue.

Mr. Dilley asked what the proposed interior height of the building is.

Planning Manager Torrico answered it is 30 feet.

Applicant, Ignacio Crespo stated he is the architect of the project. He stated the typical interior
height of the other warehouses he has designed is 34 feet but wants to be sensitive to the
neighborhood. He stated he worked with Staff and reached a compromise of a 30-foot interior.

Building & Safety Manage Beilstein stated the doors on the North side cannot open into the fire
lanes. He noted that all exits along Cataract require steps but there is a requirement to propose
as many doors as possible at grade to provide disabled access. He also asked why the overall
height of the proposed building is 41 feet if the interior is 30 feet and the maximum height of the
parapets is 5 feet 7 inches.
 DPRB Minutes  Page 4
March 23, 2023

Applicant, Ignacio Crespo stated the height increases because of the towers that will screen
mechanical equipment on the roof.

Mr. Bratt asked what is required of the Applicant in Condition No. 69.

Engineering Manager Barragan answered side lane striping is the most important thing to
prevent truck ingress from Allen Avenue and enforcement from Code Compliance and Law
Enforcement.

Mr. Bratt asked how wide the proposed driveways on Allen and Cataract Avenue are.

Engineering Manager Barragan answered they are 30 feet and 40 feet wide at the wings.

Mr. Sorcinelli asked if there are any conditions limiting the hours of operations for future tenants.

Planning Manager Torrico answered there are not because concerns of hours of operations can
be addressed by Code Compliance through the noise ordinance.

Mr. Sorcinelli stated he would be in favor of adding a condition to ease concern of the residents
on Allen Avenue.

Director of Community Development Noh asked the Applicant how soon would construction
on the project start.

Applicant, Ignacio Crespo answered as soon as possible.

There were no further comments to be heard.

Motion DPRB Case No. 21-0002 & Tree Permit 21-0004

Director of Community Development Noh moved to recommend approval to the Planning
Commission with the following additions to the Conditions of Approval;
  • The Applicant/Developer shall ensure that all doors exiting to the drive-aisle/fire lane
  comply with all applicable codes.
  • The Applicant/Developer shall install decorative, recessed-lighting or ground-mounted up-
  lighting on the recessed alcoves on the South and East elevations. Lighting fixture design
  shall be submitted to the Planning Division for review and approval.
  • All future tenants’ business operations, including but not limited to truck deliveries and
  hours of operation shall comply with the City’s noise ordinance.

Motion seconded by Mr. Dilley.

Motion carried 5-0-1 (Bratt abstain)

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Planning Manager Torrico introduced Planning Intern Miclat to the Board.
